Specifically, separatrices are traced along eigenvectors corresponding to contracting or expanding directions [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that separatrices are traced along eigenvectors corresponding to contracting or expanding directions. However, Source [S3] explicitly defines separation and attachment lines as locations where the flow direction is orthogonal to the major or minor eigenvectors of the Jacobian. Furthermore, the text states that separatrices emerging from these lines are integrated 'in the direction of flow convergence' (which relates to the flow field itself, not necessarily the eigenvectors of the boundary Jacobian in the manner described). The claim conflates the geometric definition of the starting points (orthogonality to eigenvectors) with the tracing direction, and misattributes the tracing path to the eigenvectors themselves rather than the flow convergence direction.
